settled.because: Correct when you read the repo — the evidence job had never run because doctor.yml only merged that evening. It now runs daily (05:10 UTC cron) and commits doctor/evidence.json + backlog; today's runs prove it (commits f0766789, 26fbc707). Your 'make absence a visible failure' ask is half-done: the commit step warns rather than fails. If you still see a stale evidence.json after 2026-08-07, re-file with new_evidence_since.

Verified and fixed the same day. showrunner_review.py's header and two docstrings said infra failures are 'treated as ship by callers' — stale since shared/showrunner_gate.py centralized the policy. They now say: review raises on infra failure, and the shared gate decides — open on preview, CLOSED on publish.

Verified REAL and HIGH — good catch, exactly what this loop is for. decide() blocked only on the literal token 'block' or a missing score, so {'verdict':'error','score':7} shipped on a publish run. Now on publish nothing ships except literally verdict='ship' with a numeric score in [0,100] (the reviewer's actual scale — your 'bounded' ask, calibrated to compute_score); every unknown/malformed shape holds. Ten adversarial cases in tests/test_showrunner_gate.py::TestOnlyAnExplicitShipShips. Rubric/version metadata validation deliberately deferred — the reviewer doesn't emit it yet; adding a required field the producer doesn't produce would block every real video.

The diagnosis is right — decide_verdict() in the reviewer and decide() in the gate both claim final authority — and the direction you propose (reviewer returns measurements + anchored judgments; ONE policy function computes the only disposition) is the same direction the 2026-08-01 gate extraction was already moving. But it's a refactor across every publishing channel's callsite, and this week the priority is watching the new backfill/cap/backoff machinery hold in production. Constraint for whoever picks it up: the consolidation may only ever ADD blocks — the sovereign-BLOCK and fail-closed tests must pass unchanged.

Confirmed: engines/render_qa.py (fail-open on analyzer error) and shared/video_qa.py (fail-closed) are two independent finished-video QA engines with different semantics, used by different channels (trending vs third capture). Consolidating them safely needs parity fixtures across both channels before either implementation can be retired — real risk of silently changing what ships if rushed. Parking as long_term; not something to build in a single triage session.

Confirmed real: judge_loop.run is unwired (scripts/produce.py only imports its lower-level helpers -- run_judges/combine/compare/next_escalation -- never .run itself), and it has drifted from produce.py's path in two ways: JudgingStore.open_attempt() hashes the artifact BEFORE render_fn runs, and a failed render is written to the store but never added to the verdicts dict decide() sees, so three passing required judges can yield advance=True even when render_fn returned ok=false. Real bug, but the actual fix is an architecture call (converge produce.py onto judge_loop.run vs. formally retire judge_loop.run and migrate its useful comparison/escalation logic) that deserves a dedicated session, not a rushed patch competing with today's one-item budget. Parking 30 days; revisit after items 1-3 land.

This is genuinely a 'ways out' architectural cleanup (version the contract around one map + shared accessor), not urgent against three higher-severity items filed the same day. Revisit if a future finding shows the two fields actually diverging in production.
